statement: Whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r, let a_1 < a_2 < ... < a_k be the k smallest positive integers x such that no index i with 0 <= i < len(nums) has nums[i] = x. Then r = a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_k.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000. All arithmetic in the statement is mathematical integer arithmetic.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, go out of bounds, or overflow.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r, r >= k*(k+1)/2.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r, r <= k*len(nums) + k*(k+1)/2.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: Let m be the k-th smallest positive integer that does not occur in nums. Whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r, r = m*(m+1)/2 - sum of d over the set D, where D is the set of distinct integers d such that 1 <= d <= m and there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = d.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: Suppose there is an integer a with 0 <= a such that every integer 1,2,...,a occurs as some nums[i], and no integer a+1,a+2,...,a+k occurs as any nums[i]. Then whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r, r = k*(2*a+k+1)/2, equivalently r = sum from j=1 to k of (a+j).
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: If every positive integer that occurs as an entry of nums1 also occurs as an entry of nums2, then whenever minimal_k_sum(nums1, k) returns r1 and minimal_k_sum(nums2, k) returns r2, r1 <= r2.
preconditions: nums1 and nums2 are slices of 64-bit integers, each with 1 <= length <= 100000 and all entries between 1 and 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: If, for every positive integer x, x occurs as an entry of nums1 if and only if x occurs as an entry of nums2, then whenever minimal_k_sum(nums1, k) returns r1 and minimal_k_sum(nums2, k) returns r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: nums1 and nums2 are slices of 64-bit integers, each with 1 <= length <= 100000 and all entries between 1 and 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r, r = k*(k+1)/2 if and only if no value x with 1 <= x <= k occurs as an entry of nums.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k) returns a result r, there exists a finite set A of positive integers such that |A| = k, no element of A is equal to any nums[i], the sum of all a in A equals r, and every positive integer x that is not in A and does not occur in nums is greater than every element of A.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k is a 64-bit integer with 1 <= k <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever minimal_k_sum(nums, k1) returns r1 and minimal_k_sum(nums, k2) returns r2, r1 <= r2. Moreover, if k1 < k2 then r1 < r2.
preconditions: nums is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; k1 and k2 are 64-bit integers with 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 100000000.
